stem: Before any rumours, a target's shares traded at USD 32. Takeover speculation pushed the price to USD 36 the day before a formal cash offer of USD 41.60 per share was announced. The takeover premium is closest to:
explanation: Premium is measured against the unaffected price: (41.60 − 32) / 32 = 30.00%.

rationale.A: Incorrect. 15.56% uses the rumour-inflated price of 36, which already embeds part of the premium.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 23.08% divides the premium of 9.60 by the offer price instead of the unaffected price.

stem: An acquirer has net income of USD 150 million, 50 million shares and a share price of USD 60. It offers USD 15 per share, paid entirely in its own stock at the current price, for all 25 million shares of a target earning USD 20 million. Ignoring synergies, the combined company's EPS is closest to:
explanation: Shares issued = (15 × 25m) / 60 = 6.25m. Combined EPS = (150 + 20) / (50 + 6.25) = 3.02, up from 3.00 because the acquirer's P/E of 20 exceeds the 18.75 P/E it pays.

rationale.A: Incorrect. 3.40 = 170 / 50 ignores the new shares issued to target shareholders.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 2.27 = 170 / 75 assumes one acquirer share is issued per target share instead of using the exchange ratio.

stem: A target has a standalone market value of USD 400 million. An acquirer pays USD 460 million in cash for it and expects synergies with a present value of USD 100 million. The gain to the acquirer's shareholders (in USD millions) is closest to:

rationale.A: Correct. Synergies of 100 less the 60 premium paid = 40.
rationale.B: Incorrect. 60 is the premium, which is the target shareholders' gain.
rationale.C: Incorrect. 100 is total synergies; it ignores the premium paid away to the target.

stem: A parent company wants to separate a fast-growing software unit, raise cash for itself and keep majority control of the unit. The structure that best meets all three goals is:
explanation: In an equity carve-out the parent sells a minority stake in the subsidiary through an IPO, raising cash while retaining control.

rationale.A: Incorrect. A spin-off distributes subsidiary shares pro rata to existing shareholders and raises no cash.
rationale.B: Correct. Selling a minority stake to the public raises cash and keeps control.
rationale.C: Incorrect. A split-off exchanges subsidiary shares for parent shares; it raises no cash and typically gives up the unit.
